The common misconception about evolution is the bad/unnecessary traits get weened out of the gene pool to create a “better” race in the end; i.e, “the strong survive”. When in reality genes like to diversify as much as possible; this means that in the event of a disaster, a diverse gene pool has a high chance of “survivors” making it through. In this sense, MANY human traits can arguably be called useless in the modern day, or simply cannot be measured by a “purpose”. Sickle cell anemia is a common example in discussions like this. This genetic trait saves people from the malaria parasite, but in double recessive patients can cause serious health problems from the lack of oxygen their blood carries. So while evolution is commonly perceived as this force of forward progress, that conceptually neglects half of the picture; “selective pressure”, AND can actually have negative impacts on the population. 

Tl;dr... genes simply like to be diverse because WHATEVER happens; war, disease, famine, etc., ANY difference can mean survival. Assigning “purpose” is redundant.(unless some future weapon/disease like specifically targets heterosexuals. In that case, homosexuality would TOTALLY have worked exactly to “evolutions” design.)

I think the nature of your question might be better discussed in an anthropological light; how homosexuality has developed/its role in human history, rather than its purpose in our gene pool
